<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Item&nbsp;1. Business</font></b><a name="Item1_Business_074705"></a></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Overview</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="line-height:11.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We are</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">  </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">a</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">  </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">global</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">  </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">biopharmaceutical</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">  </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">company</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">  </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">currently</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">  </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">focused</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">  </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">on</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">  </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">commercializing</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">  </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">our</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">  </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">antibiotic</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">  </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">product DIFICID&#174; (fidaxomicin) tablets in the United States and Canada, and developing other fidaxomicin products in the United States and worldwide, both by ourselves and with our partners and licensees.&#160; DIFICID, a macrolide antibacterial drug, was approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, or FDA, on May&nbsp;27, 2011, for the treatment of <i>Clostridium difficile</i>-associated diarrhea, or CDAD, in adults 18 years of age and older. CDAD is the most common symptom of <i>Clostridium difficile</i> infection, or CDI.&#160; We market DIFICID in the United States through our own sales force and through our co-promotion agreement with Cubist Pharmaceuticals,&nbsp;Inc., or Cubist.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We continue to pursue regulatory approval for, and commercialization of, fidaxomicin in other geographies outside the United States and Canada through various collaboration partners.&#160; DIFICLIR</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">TM</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;(fidaxomicin) is approved in Europe for the treatment of adults suffering from CDI.&#160; In June&nbsp;2012, our collaboration partner, Astellas Pharma Europe Ltd., or APEL, achieved the first sales of DIFICLIR in certain of its European territories.&#160; In June&nbsp;2012, our subsidiary, Optimer Pharmaceuticals Canada,&nbsp;Inc., or Optimer Canada, began marketing DIFICID in Canada. We have entered into agreements with Astellas Pharma Inc., or Astellas Japan, and with Specialised Therapeutics Australia Pty. Ltd, or STA, for the development and commercialization of fidaxomicin in Japan and in Australia and New Zealand, respectively.&#160; In November&nbsp;2012, we entered an exclusive agreement with AstraZeneca UK Limited, or AstraZeneca, to commercialize fidaxomicin for the treatment of CDI in Latin America, including Brazil, Central America, Mexico and the Caribbean.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:39.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">CDAD </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">is the most common nosocomial, or hospital acquired, diarrhea and is a significant medical problem in hospitals and long-term care facilities. In addition, CDAD is beginning to emerge in the community among people previously at low risk for the disease.&#160; CDAD is a serious illness resulting from infection of the inner lining of the colon&nbsp;by<i> C. difficile</i>&nbsp;bacteria, which produce toxins that cause inflammation of the colon, severe diarrhea and, in the most serious cases, death.&#160; Certain subpopulations, such as older patients, transplant patients, patients taking concomitant antibiotics and cancer patients, are at a higher risk of contracting CDAD.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:39.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">DIFICID is the first drug approved by the FDA for the treatment of CDAD in more than 25 years.&nbsp; In two large Phase 3 clinical trials, DIFICID reached its primary endpoint, with non-inferiority in clinical response rates at the end of treatment compared to oral vancomycin (88% vs. 86% and 88% vs. 87%, p=NS, for DIFICID and vancomycin, respectively).&#160; In addition, DIFICID was designated by the FDA as superior to vancomycin, the only other agent with an indication for the treatment of CDAD, in sustaining clinical response through 25 days beyond the end of treatment (70% vs. 57%, p=0.0011; 72% vs. 57%, p=0.0004, for DIFICID and vancomycin, respectively).&#160; Sustained clinical response was defined as clinical response at the end of treatment and survival without proven or suspected CDAD recurrence through the 25-day follow-up period.&#160; DIFICID is the only FDA-approved antibacterial drug proven to be superior to vancomycin in sustained clinical response for CDAD.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">3<a name="PB_3_074733_5335"></a></font></p>
<div style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="left"></div>
</div>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Recurrence rates in the Phase 3 clinical trials among patients who had initial clinical response were statistically significantly lower in those treated with DIFICID.&#160; In the modified intention-to-treat, or mITT, population, recurrence rates were 15.4% for DIFICID versus 25.3% for vancomycin (p<i>=</i>0.005) in one trial and 12.7% for DIFICID versus 26.9% for vancomycin (p=0.0002) in the other trial.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In August&nbsp;2012, the Centers for Medicare&nbsp;&amp; Medicaid Services, or CMS, granted a new technology add-on payment, or NTAP, for DIFICID administered in the inpatient hospital setting to treat qualifying Medicare Part A patient cases with CDAD.&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Introduced in 2001, the add-on payment is designed to support timely access to innovative therapies used to treat Medicare beneficiaries in the inpatient setting that provide a substantial clinical improvement over existing therapies.&#160; Acute care hospitals participating in the inpatient prospective payment system are eligible for an additional reimbursement of up to $868 per case in fiscal year 2013 where cost of the entire case exceeds the Medicare Severity Diagnosis Related Group payment amount.&#160; The DIFICID add-on payment granted by CMS represents a policy change, as DIFICID is the first, and only, oral medication not associated with a procedure code ever approved for an NTAP.&#160; The add-on payment is a special additional payment for qualifying Medicare cases and is intended to assist in addressing cost as a barrier to appropriate use.&#160; The policy is effective for hospital discharges occurring on or after October&nbsp;1, 2012 and will continue for two to three years.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Subject to&nbsp;FDA&nbsp;discussion and review, we intend to pursue new areas where we perceive opportunities exist to expand the DIFICID label to include new indications.&#160; We believe prophylactic use of DIFICID represents a potential opportunity for significant incremental market expansion.&nbsp; For example, in October&nbsp;2012, we initiated a Phase 3 clinical trial for the prevention of CDAD in patients undergoing hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, or HSCT, which is often referred to as bone marrow transplantation.&#160; CDAD can be a serious complication of HCST, leading to longer hospital stays and increased cost of care.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We were incorporated in November&nbsp;1998.&#160; In addition to Optimer Canada, we established subsidiaries in Bermuda and Europe in 2012 to facilitate our international expansion.&#160; We sold our remaining interest in OBI Pharma,&nbsp;Inc., formerly known as Optimer Biotechnology,&nbsp;Inc, or OBI, in 2012 for $60.0 million in gross proceeds.&#160;&#160; In this report, &#147;Optimer Pharmaceuticals,&#148; &#147;Optimer,&#148; &#147;we,&#148; &#147;us&#148; and &#147;our&#148; refer to Optimer Pharmaceuticals,&nbsp;Inc., Optimer Canada and our other international subsidiaries on a consolidated basis, unless the context otherwise requires.&#160; Our principal executive offices are in Jersey City, New Jersey, and we operate a facility in San Diego, California.&#160; We maintain an internet website at <i>www.optimerpharma.com</i>, which includes links to reports we have filed with the SEC.&#160; Any information that is included on, or linked to, our internet site is not a part of this report or any registration statement that incorporates this report by reference.&#160; Our filings may be read and copied at the SEC&#146;s Public Reference Room&nbsp;at 100&nbsp;F Street, NE, Washington, DC 20549.&#160; Information on the operation of the Public Reference Room&nbsp;may be obtained by calling the SEC at 1-800-732-0330.&#160; The SEC maintains a website that contains reports, proxy and information statements, and other information regarding issuers that file electronically with the SEC. The address of that website is <i>www.sec.gov</i>.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Our Business Strategy</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our goal is to establish ourselves as a leading hospital specialty products-based biopharmaceutical company focused on the global commercialization of fidaxomicin.&#160; To achieve this objective, our strategy includes the following key elements:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Build a branded anti-infective franchise for DIFICID in the United States and Canada</font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">.&#160; We intend to continue the successful commercialization of DIFICID by supporting increased patient access, continuity of care, formulary access across payors, hospitals and long-term care facilities and the adoption of first-line DIFICID use in appropriate patients.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Establish collaborations and distribution arrangements in international markets.</font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> We intend to continue to secure fidaxomicin marketing authorization in markets outside the United States where <i>C. difficile</i> has emerged as a serious health problem and pursue commercialization in these markets by evaluating partnering alternatives to market our products as appropriate.&#160; To date, we have entered into collaborations with: APEL for Europe; Astellas Japan for Japan; STA for Australia and New Zealand; and AstraZeneca for Latin America.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Develop DIFICID for additional indications</font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">. We believe there are opportunities to expand DIFICID&#146;s label to address unmet medical needs related to CDI that can provide clinical benefit to patients. We plan to pursue, subject to FDA discussion and review, such opportunities which we believe have significant market expansion potential.&#160; We currently are evaluating prophylactic use of DIFICID in patients undergoing bone marrow transplantation, who are at risk for CDAD and where CDAD has a significant impact on the patient and the disease-associated burden. Other opportunities exist in oncology patients, patients with multiple recurrences of CDAD and pediatric patients.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">4<a name="PB_4_074753_5796"></a></font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Selectively acquire or in-license additional hospital specialty products for development and/or commercialization</font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">.&#160; In order to maximize the value of our hospital franchise and the investment in our commercial infrastructure, we intend to opportunistically consider the expansion of our product portfolio by selectively acquiring or in-licensing additional hospital products or product candidates. We believe the U.S. hospital market provides an opportunity for a biopharmaceutical company with a modestly sized sales infrastructure to successfully market innovative medicines.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Commercialization Efforts</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We market DIFICID in the United States through our own sales force and through our co-promotion agreement with Cubist.&#160; In 2011, we completed the establishment of our commercial infrastructure, including key additions to our senior management team, to commercialize DIFICID in the United States.&#160; Our infrastructure includes a sales force of approximately 116 hospital sales specialists, in addition to experienced commercial and marketing management.&#160; Our commercialization functions include institutional formulary adoption, payor access/coverage, sales and promotion.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our commercialization efforts are directed at physicians, pharmacists, administrators and others throughout the hospital and long-term care settings.&#160; Our primary commercial efforts are focused on the hospital, where the majority of initial prescribing decisions for DIFICID are made, as a means of driving broader use of DIFICID in other segments such as long-term care and retail.&#160; Our sales representatives primarily target approximately 1,200 hospitals, although approximately 2,750 hospitals have ordered DIFICID.&#160; In October&nbsp;2012, we instituted a hospital contracting strategy that provides a discount to hospitals for DIFICID use in the acute care inpatient setting.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On April&nbsp;5, 2011, we entered into a co-promotion agreement with Cubist, pursuant to which we engaged Cubist as our exclusive partner for the promotion of DIFICID in the United States.&nbsp; Under the terms of the agreement, Cubist and we have agreed to co-promote DIFICID to physicians, hospitals, long-term care facilities and other healthcare institutions, as well as jointly to provide medical affairs support for DIFICID.&#160; In addition to DIFICID, Cubist markets CUBICIN&#174; and ENTEREG&#174;.&#160; With the establishment of our own field force, we estimate that the vast majority of our approximately 1,200 target hospitals are covered by both a Cubist representative and an Optimer representative.&#160; As such, we currently do not anticipate renewing the co-promotion agreement when it expires on July&nbsp;31, 2013, and will evaluate expanding our field force to detail the hospitals currently covered only by a Cubist representative.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We are pursuing regulatory approval and commercialization of fidaxomicin in other geographies outside the United States and Canada through various collaboration partners.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Distribution</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We sell DIFICID through wholesalers that have agreed to be authorized distributors of record of DIFICID in the United States.&#160; These wholesalers sell DIFICID to hospitals and long-term care facilities, in addition to retail and specialty pharmacies in the United States.&#160; We outsource a number of our product supply chain services to third-party vendors, including services related to warehousing and inventory management, distribution, chargeback processing and accounts receivable management.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We introduced DIFICID Rx Assist</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">TM</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;in the third quarter of 2012 to help facilitate the process of filling patients&#146; prescriptions in the retail setting.&#160; We sell product directly to Advanced Care Scripts, or ACS, a part of Omnicare Specialty Care Group, which manages the DIFICID Rx Assist program on our behalf.&nbsp; By selling product directly to ACS, we can ensure that the DIFICID Rx Assist program has an appropriate level of inventory available to ship to patients at all times.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<div>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Our Market Opportunity</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our primary market is the U.S. hospital market, which consists of approximately 7,000 acute care hospitals.&#160; U.S. hospitals purchased over $10 billion of antibiotics in 2009. Many antibiotics used to treat infections have well-documented shortcomings. For example, certain antibiotics often fail to reach sufficient concentrations at the site of infection to adequately eliminate harmful bacteria. Certain of these antibiotics also have been associated with serious adverse side effects, including renal toxicities, heart rhythm abnormalities, phototoxicity, rashes and central nervous effects, such as seizures. These side effects limit the use of antibiotics for certain patients.&#160; In addition, certain antibiotics have interaction issues with prescribed drugs, such as cholesterol lowering agents. Safety problems can arise when increased doses of these antibiotics are needed to treat resistant bacteria. If bacteria develop resistance to currently available antibiotics, the underlying infection can become difficult or impossible to treat, and may lead to death. Patients also often fail to comply with antibiotic treatment regimens due to many factors including the inability to tolerate an antibiotic due to its side effects, inconvenient method of dosing and undesirable frequency and length of dosing. Because of these shortcomings associated with marketed antibiotics, we believe an opportunity exists to improve upon existing treatments.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Our Product and Product Candidates</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We believe that fidaxomicin offers, or may offer, advantages over existing antibiotics.&#160; We also believe that the markets for fidaxomicin present us with significant commercial opportunities.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our ability, or our licensees&#146; abilities, to obtain additional regulatory approvals for fidaxomicin may require us or our licensees to successfully complete additional clinical development and demonstrate, through data submissions, the safety and efficacy of the product candidate to the satisfaction of foreign regulatory authorities.&#160; Clinical trials involve a lengthy and expensive process with an uncertain outcome, and efficacy and safety data of earlier studies and trials may not be predictive of future trial results.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our current product or product candidate portfolio consists of the following:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<div style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><hr size="1" width="25%" noshade color="black" align="left"></div>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(1)</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We intend that data from these Phase 3 trials, if successful, will be presented to the FDA as part of an sNDA in order to expand the DIFICID label.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(2)</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">FDA requirement or commitment.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Fidaxomicin</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Overview</font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">.&#160; We developed fidaxomicin for the treatment of infection caused by <i>C.&nbsp;difficile</i> bacteria.&#160; <i>C. difficile </i></font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">is the most common cause of infectious diarrhea in healthcare settings.&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Fidaxomicin is a differentiated antibacterial drug for the treatment of CDAD in adults 18 years of age or older.&#160; CDAD is the most common symptom of <i>C. difficile</i> infection.&#160; Fidaxomicin has potent activity against <i>C. difficile </i>and moderate activity against certain other gram-positive organisms, such as<i> Enterococcus </i>and<i> Staphylococcus</i>,<i>  </i>but it is virtually inactive against Gram-negative organisms and yeast.&#160; Fidaxomicin is bactericidal <i>in vitro</i> and has a unique mechanism of action, exerting its activity by inhibiting RNA polymerase, a bacterial enzyme.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Clostridium difficile Infection</font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">. CDI has become a significant medical problem in hospitals, in long-term care facilities and in the community and is estimated to afflict more than 700,000 people each year in the United States.&nbsp; <i>C. difficile </i></font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">has surpassed methicillin-resistant </font><i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Staphylococcus aureus,</font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> or<i>  </i></font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">MRSA, as the leading cause of healthcare-acquired infections in community hospitals.&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">CDI is a serious illness resulting from infection of the inner lining of the colon by <i>C.&nbsp;difficile</i> bacteria that produce toxins causing inflammation of the colon, severe diarrhea and, in the most serious cases, death.&#160; Patients typically develop CDI from the use of broad-spectrum antibiotics that disrupt normal gastrointestinal (gut) flora, thus allowing <i>C. difficile</i> bacteria to flourish and produce toxins.&#160; <i>C. difficile</i> is a spore forming bacterium, creating spores excreted in the environment of the patients that can survive for months on dry surfaces in hospital rooms such as beds and doors, and can contaminate other patients by fecal-oral transmission through the hands of healthcare workers.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In addition to fidaxomicin, therapeutic options for CDAD include the use of metronidazole off-label and oral vancomycin, the latter being the only other agent that is FDA-approved for the treatment for CDAD.&nbsp; However, approximately 20% to 30% of CDAD patients who initially respond to these older treatment options experience a clinical recurrence following cessation of treatment.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Primary risk factors for CDI include broad-spectrum antibiotic use (such as cephalosporins and fluoroquinolones), age (over 65), immune compromised status (such as oncology patients), presence of multiple comorbidities and prolonged stay in a healthcare facility.&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Incidence and severity of CDI cases are increasing </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">with growing rates of recurrence, septic shock, toxic megacolon and intestinal perforation.&#160; <i>C. difficile</i>-associated mortality rates increased 400% between 2000 and 2007 in the United States.</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">  </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The elderly are particularly vulnerable, as o</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">ver two-thirds of CDI patients are 65 years and older.&#160; R</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">ates of morbidity and mortality increase with patient age, with a mortality rate as high as </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">14% </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">in elderly patients.&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The increasing incidence and mortality of CDI, along with high rates of both treatment failures and recurrences with earlier therapies, has resulted in greater awareness and concern about CDI among medical professionals and public health officials.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We believe that the incidence of CDI may be higher than what is reported because many hospitals are not required to and do not report incidence of CDI. According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, CDI rates increased 200% for hospitalized patients aged over 65 years from 1996 to 2009.&#160; Data published in 2012 by</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> the </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project (HCUP) showed that i</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">n 2009, there were 336,600 hospitalizations that involved CDI, which is nearly 1% of all hospital stays.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">7<a name="PB_7_080137_5796"></a></font></p>
<div style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="left"></div>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Reports indicate that the incidence of community-acquired CDI cases also may be increasing and CDI has been observed in populations previously considered to be at low risk.&#160; In one population-based U.S. study, community-acquired CDI accounted for 41% of all definite CDI cases.&#160; The same study showed that the incidence of both community-acquired and hospital-acquired CDI increased significantly over the study period.&#160; Compared to those with hospital-acquired CDI, patients with community-acquired infection were younger, more likely to be female, had lower comorbidity scores and were less likely to have severe infection or to have been exposed to antibiotics.&#160; The study demonstrated that CDI affects populations previously thought to be at low risk, including young adults and children, and those who lack the traditional risk factors of recent hospitalization or exposure to antibiotics.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Generally, CDI results in longer hospital stays and increases average patient cost which often is not fully reimbursed to the hospital. Compared to the average inpatient, CDI patients are considerably sicker and their cases more complex.&#160; Patients with CDI hospital stays are more severely ill than the general hospital population, with longer lengths-of-stay and higher death rates.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In more complicated cases of CDI, hospitalization may be prolonged by up to two weeks. One analysis showed that the adjusted mean cost for CDI cases was $15,400 higher than for cases without CDI, and the adjusted mean length of hospital stay was over eight days longer.&#160; In certain populations, such as surgical patients, the costs can be even higher and lengths of stay up to 16 days longer.&#160; The overall costs attributable to CDI cases in the U.S. healthcare system are estimated at $8.2 billion per year.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We believe that DIFICID addresses an unmet medical need for patients with CDAD and provides economic value to the healthcare system:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">DIFICID is the first drug approved by the FDA to treat CDAD in more than 25 years and</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;has demonstrated comparable initial efficacy and a superior sustained clinical response through 25 days after the end of treatment for CDAD versus vancomycin, the only other drug FDA approved drug for the treatment of CDAD.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">DIFICID is the first, and only, oral medication to qualify for a new technology add-on payment from CMS.&#160; The NTAP program is only available to new technologies demonstrating a substantial clinical improvement and meeting specific cost thresholds.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We believe DIFICID&#146;s profile provides an opportunity to develop significant market penetration for first-line use in CDAD patients.&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Additionally, we believe there are opportunities to expand DIFICID&#146;s label to address unmet medical needs related to CDAD and provide value to patients and the healthcare system.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Alternative Treatments and Limitations</font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">.&#160; Metronidazole generally is used for patients in the United States and Europe experiencing their first mild-to-moderate episode or first recurrent episode of CDAD.&#160; Metronidazole is a generic drug that is used off-label to treat CDAD due to its low cost and historical efficacy.&#160; The guideline-recommended treatment regimen for metronidazole is 500 mg three times per day, for 10 to 14 days.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Vancomycin is used in the United States and also in Europe and Japan for the treatment of CDAD.&#160; As a result of its broad antibacterial activity, intravenously administered vancomycin frequently is used for certain other life-threatening infections caused by multi-drug resistant bacteria such as MRSA.&#160; In an effort to slow the continuing emergence of vancomycin-resistant bacteria, the medical community discourages the use of the drug for the treatment of CDAD except for patients who are not responding to metronidazole, for patients with severe symptoms or for patients with risk factors that are predictive of negative treatment outcomes.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Both metronidazole and vancomycin have shortcomings as treatments for CDAD including:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Limited Efficacy.&#160; A controlled study conducted in North America and reported in 2007 showed that approximately 19% of CDAD patients treated with oral vancomycin and 28% of CDAD patients treated with metronidazole do not respond to therapy, and these patients are at risk of developing more severe CDAD.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">High Recurrence Rate.&#160; Approximately 25% of CDAD patients who initially respond to oral vancomycin and approximately 27% of CDAD patients who initially respond to metronidazole experience a clinical recurrence following the cessation of antibiotic administration.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Bacterial Resistance.&#160; Widespread use of oral vancomycin is discouraged for the treatment of CDAD in some hospitals due to concerns over the development of cross-resistant bacteria, including vancomycin-resistant <i>enterococcus</i>, or VRE, and vancomycin-resistant <i>Staphylococcus</i>, which can cause other serious nosocomial infections.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Adverse Side Effects.&#160; Metronidazole, which is systemically absorbed, may result in adverse side effects and complications, including seizures, toxic reactions to alcohol, leukopenia, neuropathy, unpleasant taste and dry mouth.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Inducement of CDI.&#160; Oral vancomycin and metronidazole are both broad-spectrum antibacterials that disrupt the normal gut <i>flora</i>, which help suppress the growth of <i>C.&nbsp;difficile</i>.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Less Convenient Dosing and Compliance.&#160; The current treatment regimen for oral vancomycin and metronidazole is less convenient, as both must be administered three or four times per day for a minimum of 10 days, which may result in lower levels of patient compliance.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">8<a name="PB_8_080216_3020"></a></font></p>
<div style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="left"></div>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Fidaxomicin Differentiating Characteristics</font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">.&#160; Fidaxomicin is a unique antibacterial drug consisting of an 18-member macrocyclic ester ring structure.&#160; After receiving expedited priority review, fidaxomicin was approved by the FDA in May&nbsp;2011 for the treatment of CDAD in adults 18 years of age or older.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Fidaxomicin has significant differentiating features, including:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">an initial response rate comparable to vancomycin and a designation by the FDA as superior in sustained clinical response (enduring response) through 25 days after the end of treatment;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">a targeted antimicrobial spectrum primarily limited to species of <i>clostridia</i>, including <i>C. difficile</i>;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">bactericidal activity against <i>C.&nbsp;difficile in vitro</i>;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">limited disruption of normal gut <i>flora</i> both <i>in vitro</i> and in fecal profiling clinical studies, which may contribute to the lower likelihood of CDAD recurrence;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">lower risk of colonization by VRE with fidaxomicin (7%) than vancomycin (31%);</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">minimal systemic absorption, acting locally in the gastrointestinal tract;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">post-antibiotic effect of 6 to 10 hours;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">twice daily dosing regimen;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">no <i>in vitro</i> cross-resistance with other classes of antibacterial drugs; and</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">no significant drug interactions, no contra-indications and no dose adjustment necessary in patients over 65 years old or in patients with renal or hepatic impairment.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Clinical Development</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Phase&nbsp;3 Pivotal Trials</font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">DIFICID is the first drug approved by the FDA for the treatment of CDAD in more than 25 years.&#160; In two large Phase 3 clinical trials, DIFICID reached its primary endpoint successfully, with non-inferiority in clinical response rates at the end of treatment compared to oral vancomycin (88% vs. 86% and 88% vs. 87%, p=NS, for DIFICID and vancomycin respectively).&#160; In addition, DIFICID was designated by the FDA as superior to vancomycin, the only other agent with an indication for the treatment of CDAD, in sustaining clinical response through 25 days beyond the end of treatment (70% vs. 57%, p=0.0011; 72% vs. 57%, p=0.0004, for DIFICID and vancomycin respectively).&#160; Sustained clinical response was defined as clinical response at the end of treatment and survival without proven or suspected CDAD recurrence through the 25-day follow-up period.&#160; DIFICID is the only FDA-approved antibacterial drug proven to be superior to vancomycin in sustained clinical response for CDAD.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Recurrence rates in the Phase 3 clinical trials among patients who had initial clinical response were statistically significantly lower in those treated with DIFICID.&#160; In the modified intention-to-treat population, recurrence rates were 15% for DIFICID versus 25% for vancomycin (p=0.0005) in one trial and 13% for DIFICID versus 27% for vancomycin (p=0.0002) in the other trial.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Results from the Phase 3 trials are summarized below:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Further analysis of the results from the Phase 3 trials and several recent publications demonstrated other potential advantages of fidaxomicin:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">in patients with more pronounced diarrhea (diarrhea that did not resolve in the first 24 hours of therapy), fidaxomicin was associated with a faster time to resolution than vancomycin (79 hours vs. 105 hours, p=0.056);</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">in patients who did not receive either vancomycin or metronidazole in the 24-hour pre-trial enrollment period, the difference in recurrence rate between fidaxomicin and vancomycin was more pronounced than in the overall patient population at 10.9% vs. 24.3%, respectively;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">CDI recurrence occurred significantly later in patients treated with fidaxomicin with only 3% and 9% recurrence rates versus 14% and 20% recurrence rates for vancomycin, at 10 and 20 days post-treatment, respectively;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">fidaxomicin was less likely than vancomycin to promote VRE colonization in patients treated for CDI, which we believe may be due to inhibitory activity of fidaxomicin against many VRE strains and fidaxomicin&#146;s relative sparing of the intestinal <i>flora</i> including <i>Bacteroides </i>bacteria.&#160; The analysis showed that only 7% of patients treated with fidaxomicin acquired VRE versus 31% of vancomycin-treated patients (p&lt;0.001);</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">fidaxomicin was significantly more effective than vancomycin in achieving clinical cure in the presence of concomitant antibiotics, or CA, therapy and in preventing recurrence regardless of CA use;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">a meta-analysis of the two pivotal trials showed that in the full analysis set (ITT population), fidaxomicin reduced persistent diarrhea, recurrence or death by 40% (95% confidence interval [CI], 26%&#151;51%; p &lt; .0001) compared with vancomycin through day 40.&#160; Through day 12, fidaxomicin reduced persistent diarrhea or death by 37%; and</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">fidaxomicin is able to inhibit <i>C. difficile&#146;s</i> production of spores, the most readily transmissible form of <i>C. difficile</i>, <i>in vitro</i> and that fidaxomicin inhibits toxin production by <i>C. difficile</i>  <i>in vitro</i>.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We expect to continue to support peer reviewed publication of additional data and analyses related to fidaxomicin, as well as presentation of such data and analyses at a variety of medical and scientific meetings and conferences.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Clinical Studies/Label Expansion</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:39.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In 2012, we initiated two new clinical studies of DIFICID.&#160; The first is a Phase 2a open-label, uncontrolled, safety, tolerability and pharmacokinetic study in pediatric subjects with CDI (NCT01591863).&#160; This study is intended to recruit 32 subjects ranging in age from six months to 18 years.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We believe there are opportunities to expand DIFICID&#146;s label to address unmet medical needs related to CDI that can provide economic value to the healthcare system.&#160; We plan to pursue, subject to&nbsp;FDA&nbsp;discussion and review, such opportunities where we view significant potential for market expansion.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">One area that we believe presents an important label expansion opportunity is the prophylactic use of DIFICID in certain patient populations.&#160; We believe DIFICID may be effective not only for treating CDAD, but also in preventing CDAD in patients at high risk of developing CDAD.&#160; There currently is no therapeutic drug approved for the prevention of CDAD.&#160; We believe fidaxomicin may provide safe, potent and narrow-spectrum bactericidal activity against <i>C. difficile</i>, thereby protecting high-risk patients while limiting disruption to normal, beneficial gut <i>flora</i>.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The second study initiated in 2012 is a Phase 3b, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, controlled clinical trial comparing fidaxomicin to placebo in the prophylaxis of CDI in subjects undergoing HSCT and receiving fluoroquinolone prophylaxis (NCT01691248).&#160; Subjects undergoing HSCT will be treated once-daily with fidaxomicin 200 mg for up to 40 days (through seven days post-engraftment or past the end of fluoroquinolone prophylaxis, whichever is later).&#160; The primary endpoint is occurrence of CDI through 30 days post-treatment.&#160; The secondary endpoint is occurrence of CDI through 60 days post-treatment.&#160; This study is expected to enroll approximately 340 patients but may be readjusted for size in a blinded interim analysis at 50% enrollment.&#160; HSCT patients generally are at risk for CDAD, and CDAD has a significant impact on the patient and the disease-associated cost burden.&#160; This study was initiated in October&nbsp;2012.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">License from Par Pharmaceuticals,&nbsp;Inc.</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In February&nbsp;2007, we repurchased the rights to develop and commercialize fidaxomicin in North America and Israel from Par under a prospective buy-back agreement.&nbsp; We paid Par a $5.0 million milestone payment in June&nbsp;2010 for the successful completion of our second pivotal Phase&nbsp;3 trial for fidaxomicin.&nbsp; We are obligated to pay Par a 5% royalty on any net sales by us, our affiliates or our licensees of fidaxomicin in North America and Israel, including Cubist, and a 1.5% royalty on any net sales by us or our affiliates of fidaxomicin in the rest of the world.&nbsp; In addition, we are required to pay Par a 6.25% royalty on net revenues we receive related to fidaxomicin in connection with the licensing of our right to market fidaxomicin in the rest of the world, such as the licenses we have granted to our partners in territories outside the United States and Canada.&nbsp; We are obligated to pay each of these royalties, if any, on a country-by-country basis for seven years commencing on the applicable commercial launch in each such country.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Other Product Candidates</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We have out-licensed rights to two development programs.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Solithromycin (CEM-101): Macrolide and Ketolide Antibiotics</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Macrolide antibiotics are marketed for the treatment of upper and lower respiratory tract infections, or RTIs.&#160; Macrolides, such as erythromycin and azithromycin, and ketolides, such as telithromycin, are related classes of antibiotics which have strong gram-positive activity and inhibit bacterial growth.&#160; However, an increasing number of pathogens is now resistant to currently available macrolides and ketolides.&#160; The leading product candidate developed by us, solithromycin, was effective against these resistant bacterial strains according to a preclinical study conducted by the Institute for Medical Microbiology.&#160; Cempra Pharmaceuticals,&nbsp;Inc., or Cempra, has licensed from us a library of approximately 500 macrolides related to this product candidate.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">CEM-101 has been shown to possess potent activity against multi-drug resistant <i>Streptococcus pneumoniae</i> and <i>Streptococcus pyogenes</i>, common RTI pathogens.&#160; A preclinical study showed that solithromycin was orally active with potent efficacy in animal models after once-a-day administration.&#160; Cempra recently initiated a global Phase 3 clinical trial of orally-administered solithromycin in patients with community-acquired bacterial pneumonia.&#160; In Phase 2 trials, solithromycin showed a favorable safety profile in over 400 patients.&#160; We may receive milestone payments as product candidates are developed and/or co-developed by Cempra, in addition to milestone payments based on certain sublicense revenue.&#160; The aggregate potential amount of such milestone payments is not capped and, based in part on the number of products developed under the agreement, may exceed $24.5 million.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">OPT-822/821: Cancer Immunotherapy for Breast Cancer</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In 2009, under an intellectual property assignment and license agreement, we assigned to OBI certain of our patent rights and know-how related to OPT-822/821, a novel carbohydrate-based cancer immunotherapy which we licensed from Memorial Sloan-Kettering Cancer Center.&#160; OBI is developing OPT-822/821 for the treatment of metastatic breast cancer.&#160; In December&nbsp;2010, OBI initiated a Phase 2/3 clinical trial of OPT-822/821 with sites in Taiwan, South Korea, Hong Kong and Malaysia.&#160; The Phase 2/3 trial is expected to enroll up to 343 patients and the primary endpoint is the progression-free survival rate from the time of randomization until disease progression.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under the intellectual property assignment and license agreement with OBI, we may receive up to $10.0 million in milestone payments for each product developed, and we also are eligible to receive royalties on net sales of any product commercialized under the program.&#160; In January&nbsp;2012, OBI and we executed a letter of agreement which provided us the right of first refusal if OBI or one of its affiliates receives any offer to obtain an exclusive, royalty-bearing license (including the right to sublicense) under the OPT-822/821 patents and the OPT-822/821 technology to develop, make, have made, use, sell, offer for sale, have sold and import OPT-822/821 products in the United States, Europe or other specified territories.&#160; In the letter of agreement, as consideration for the grant of the right of first refusal, we waived certain of OBI&#146;s obligations under the intellectual property assignment and license agreement.&#160; The letter of agreement expires 10 years from the effective date of the agreement.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Collaborations, Commercial and License Agreements</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">AstraZeneca UK Limited.</font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160; In November&nbsp;2012, we entered an exclusive distribution and license agreement with AstraZeneca to commercialize fidaxomicin for the treatment of CDI in Latin America, including Brazil, Central America, Mexico and the Caribbean.&#160; Under the terms of the agreement, we will provide to AstraZeneca the completed preclinical and clinical data, regulatory information and documents, testing information, protocols and any know-how relating to fidaxomicin.&#160; In addition to the transfer of know-how, we will provide drug product for purposes of conducting validation testing in connection with seeking regulatory approval in the covered </font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
